equation_request.abstract:
We consider the Unitary Permutation problem which consists, given $n$ unitary gates $U_{1},\ldots,U_{n}$ and a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, in applying the unitary gates in the order specified by $\sigma$, i.e. in performing $U_{\sigma(n)}\circ\ldots\circ U_{\sigma(1)}$.

This problem has been introduced and investigated in [7] where two models of computations are considered. This first is the (standard) model of query complexity: the complexity measure is the number of calls to any of the unitary gates $U_{i}$ in a quantum circuit which solves the problem. The second model provides quantum switches and treats unitary transformations as inputs of second order. In that case the complexity measure is the number of quantum switches. In their paper, Colnaghi et al. [7] have shown that the problem can be solved within $n^{2}$ calls in the query model and $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$ quantum switches in the new model.

We refine these results by proving that $n\log_{2}(n)+\Theta(n)$ quantum switches are necessary and sufficient to solve this problem, whereas $n^{2}-2n+4$ calls are sufficient to solve this problem in the standard quantum circuit model. We prove, with an additional assumption on the family of gates used in the circuits, that $n^{2}-o(n^{7/4+\epsilon})$ queries are required, for any $\epsilon>0$. The upper and lower bounds for the standard quantum circuit model are established by pointing out connections with the permutation as substring problem introduced by Karp.

specification.problem: Unitary Permutation: given black-box unitaries U_1..U_n and a permutation sigma of {1..n}, implement U_{sigma(n)} ∘ ... ∘ U_{sigma(1)}. The abstract states complexity bounds (quantum switches and queries) but not the circuit constructions.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Specify the problem itself and the stated complexity bounds, plus a tiny assumed instance (n=3, sigma=(2,3,1)) to fix conventions. The switch-based and query-based circuit constructions, the lower-bound proofs, and the link to Karp's permutation-as-substring problem are outside scope because the abstract does not give them.

symbols.domain: unitary on a fixed d-dimensional system, i in {1..n}

symbols.meaning: number of queries sufficient in the standard circuit model

equations.label: Target unitary
equations.description: Composition of the gates in the order given by sigma; U_{sigma(1)} is applied first.
equations.justification: Stated directly as the goal of the problem.

equations.label: Switch complexity
equations.description: Necessary and sufficient number of quantum switches.
equations.abstract_quote: $n\log_{2}(n)+\Theta(n)$ quantum switches are necessary and sufficient
assumptions: Switch model as in the cited prior work; its precise definition is not given.

equations.label: Query upper bound
equations.description: Number of calls sufficient in the standard circuit model.

equations.label: Query lower bound
equations.description: Lower bound on queries under an additional unspecified assumption on the gate family.
assumptions: The additional gate-family assumption is not specified in the abstract.

equations.label: Toy instance
equations.description: Example fixing the ordering convention: U_2 is applied first, then U_3, then U_1.
equations.justification: Tiny instance chosen to fix conventions.
assumptions: Instance chosen by the reconstruction, not from the abstract.
